title: Optimal truthful approximation for multi-hospital kidney exchange
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Determine the optimal worst-case expected approximation ratio for truthful two-way kidney-exchange mechanisms with arbitrarily many hospitals allowed to hide vertices.
definitions:
An instance is a finite simple undirected compatibility graph G=(V,E) with a labeled partition V=V_1⊔…⊔V_h, h≥1, into hospital-owned vertices. Each vertex represents one donor-patient pair; an edge permits a two-way exchange. Hospital i may report any R_i⊆V_i but may not invent vertices or alter edges among reported vertices. The mechanism sees only the induced graph on ⋃R_i and its ownership labels, and selects a distribution over matchings of this reported graph, with no payments. Randomization is unrestricted and no computational limit is imposed.

For a realized matching M, let V(M) be its endpoints. Hospital i obtains utility u_i(M)=|V_i∩V(M)|+2ν(G[V_i\V(M)]), where ν is maximum matching cardinality. Thus it may optimally match all its remaining own vertices internally after seeing M, including hidden vertices and unmatched reported vertices. Truthfulness in expectation requires that for every graph, partition, reports R_−i of other hospitals, and subset R_i⊆V_i, reporting all V_i gives expected utility at least that obtained by reporting R_i, with the same true graph used in both utilities. The mechanism must internally complete its returned matching: no edge may join two unmatched reported vertices of the same hospital. This makes all postprocessing utility under full truthful reports already included in the returned matching.

Define R_K as the infimum c≥1 for which one mechanism family for all finite graphs and hospital counts satisfies the incentive condition and E[|M|]≥ν(G)/c under full truthful reporting. If ν(G)=0 the welfare inequality is automatically satisfied. Since every matched edge saves two patients, comparing edges or matched vertices gives the same ratio. The unrestricted number h is part of the worst case; there is no stochastic blood-type model.
answer_criterion: Supply a real approximation a to the defined optimal constant and a complete Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most 1/100. A certified interval of width at most 1/50 qualifies via its midpoint. Exact identification is welcome but not required; an infimum or supremum need not be attained.
context: Mix-and-Match supplies a factor-two randomized truthful mechanism. Improvements for exactly two hospitals do not establish the unrestricted-hospital optimum.
why: The ratio quantifies the welfare cost of strategic participation by institutions in exchange networks.

import_provenance.original_title: The optimal truthful approximation for multi-hospital kidney exchange
import_provenance.original_statement: What is the best worst-case approximation ratio attainable by a randomized mechanism truthful in expectation for two-way kidney exchange with arbitrarily many hospitals? Hospitals own vertex sets, maximize their own matched patients, and may hide vertices and match them internally with their remaining unmatched vertices.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The paper gives factor 2 and a randomized impossibility bound of 8/7; the deterministic factor-2 lower bound does not settle the randomized question. The target concerns two-cycles and unrestricted hospital counts, not the better-understood two-hospital case.

context_blocks.text: Mix-and-Match supplies a factor-two randomized truthful mechanism. Improvements for exactly two hospitals do not establish the unrestricted-hospital optimum.

sentences: Hospitals control disjoint sets of vertices in a compatibility graph.
They may hide vertices before the mechanism selects exchanges.
A hospital can internally match its own unmatched vertices afterward.
Truthfulness compares its expected total matched patients under full disclosure and every hiding deviation.
The approximation ratio must cover arbitrarily many hospitals.
